'''Grace Elizabeth Bates''' (13 August 1914 – 19 November 1996) was an American mathematician and one of few women in the United States to be granted a Ph.D. in mathematics in the 1940s. She became an [[emeritus professor]] at [[Mount Holyoke College]].  Bates specialized in [[algebra]] and [[probability theory]], and she co-authored two textbooks: ''The Real Number System'' and ''Modern Algebra, Second Course''.<ref name=AWS/>  Throughout her own education, Bates overcame obstructions to her pursuit of knowledge, opening the way for future women learners.<ref name=womensucceeding>{{cite book|last=Bart|first=Jody|title=Women Succeeding in the Sciences: Theories and Practices Across Disciplines|year=2000|publisher=Purdue University Press|location=United States of America|isbn=1-55753-121-8|pages=46–82|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=baK6XSXhrS8C&pg=PA46}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
She was born on 13 August 1914.<ref name=AMS>{{citation |journal=Notices of the AMS |title=Deaths |volume=44 |number=3 |page=352 |year=1997}}</ref> Interested in mathematics from a very young age, Bates was encouraged to pursue her interest by her family.<ref name=womensucceeding/> Bates maintained a close relationship with her brother, reinforced by the early death of their mother. Upon completing high school, her brother used his salary to help her continue her education through high school and college.<ref name=womenbecome>{{cite book|last=Murray|first=Margaret Anne Marie|title=Women Becoming Mathematicians|year=2001|publisher=Massachusetts Institute of Technology|location=United States of America|isbn=0-262-13369-5|pages=44–99|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Sz78C8-PGUQC&pg=PA95}}</ref>

During her studies, Bates petitioned several times to take more advanced math courses than were typically available to female students.  She attended the [[Cazenovia Seminary]] for high school, where she petitioned to take intermediate algebra.<ref name="womensucceeding" /> She pursued her undergraduate studies at [[Middlebury College]], which was [[single-sex education|segregated by sex]] at this time.  For her senior year, Bates petitioned to take [[differential equation]]s, which was only offered to male students.<ref name="womensucceeding" />{{Rp|54:55}}  After completing her B.S. in mathematics in 1935, she continued in her studies to obtain a master's degree from [[Brown University]] in 1938.<ref name="womensucceeding" />

Bates entered her doctoral program at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]] in 1944.<ref name="womensucceeding" />{{Rp|80}} Initially interested in [[geometry]], Bates instead decided to pursue algebra and work under [[Reinhold Baer]].  She completed her doctoral thesis, titled "[[Free loop|Free Loops]] and [[Net (mathematics)|Nets]] and their Generalizations", in 1946.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=3937|title=Grace Bates - The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2018-09-25}}</ref>

==Professional life and continuing education==
Bates taught briefly at [[Sweet Briar College]] before joining the faculty of [[Mount Holyoke College]].  After discussing her interest in probability and statistics with colleague [[Antoni Zygmund]], Zygmund referred her to [[Jerzy Neyman]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].  Consequently, Bates obtained an assistantship at the Berkeley Statistical Laboratory and spend several summers working with Neyman in the 1950s.  Together they wrote a number of research articles on probability theory.<ref name=womensucceeding/><ref name="womenbecome" />

Bates advanced to become a full and emeritus professor at Mount Holyoke College and taught until her retirement in 1979.<ref name="womensucceeding" />  She died on 19 November 1996.<ref name="AWS">{{citation |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=gPGZJ_YuMwgC&pg=PA218 |pages=218–219 |chapter=Bates, Grace Elizabeth |title=American Women of Science Since 1900 |volume=1. A-H |author=Tiffany K. Wayne |publisher=ABC-CLIO |year=2011 |isbn=9781598841589}}</ref><ref name="AMS" /><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=eDVBDwAAQBAJ&q=grace+bates+math&pg=PA97|title=Women in Mathematics: Celebrating the Centennial of the Mathematical Association of America|last1=Beery|first1=Janet L.|author1-link=Janet Beery|last2=Greenwald|first2=Sarah J.|last3=Jensen-Vallin|first3=Jacqueline A.|last4=Mast|first4=Maura B.|author4-link=Maura Mast|date=2017-12-02|publisher=Springer|isbn=9783319666945|language=en}}</ref>
